newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgut share issue seen part of ADR scheme-traders.
newsitem.headline: Surgut share issue seen part of ADR scheme-traders.

text.p: An expected issue of preference shares in AO Surgutneftegaz may be used in the company's programme to launch American Depository Receipts, Russian stock traders said.
"It is logical. The company will issue shares, announce that they are in circulation on the market and will issue ADRs on these shares," Dmitry Lobanov of Alfa Kapital told Reuters.
Surgutneftegaz shareholders voted over the weekend to raise the number of announced shares, thus raising charter capital to 6.16 trillion roubles from 6.0 trillion.
But the actual additional issue of 166 million preference shares with face value of 1,000 roubles will take place only after it has been approved by the board of directors.
Andrei Serebryakov, head of securities at NK Surgutneftegaz oil firm, which controls about three-quarters of AO Surgutneftegaz, declined to disclose the aim of the issue or give details of placement.
"We need shares to attract investment. I would not link it to our ADR programme for preference stock," he said.
But Yuri Agaronik of Prospekt investment company said the preference shares issue would speed up the planned ADR issue.

"After the decision to issue the shares is approved, we may see ADRs very soon," he said. "The other but less likely option is that the company needs new shares for conversion of AO shares into the holding shares."
The company announced plans to issue ADRs on preference shares last December. It launched ADRs on ordinary shares in January.

The shareholders' meeting also voted to allow existing shareholders to be the first to bid for new share issues, the press service said. Shareholders may use this privilege proportionally to the number of voting shares held.
The decision was passed following recommendations from the Federal Securities Commission.
